name: ok_file_revert
description: file/revert, the record that a person put a file back to the bytes git has committed, discarding a working-tree change. It is a separate type from file/write because the two rows describe different actions even though both move bytes: file/write says a person wrote this buffer, file/revert says a person asked for the committed version. A log that could not tell them apart would leave 'who changed this file last, and did they mean to' unanswerable. A revert only succeeds for a path with a committed version; refusals (untracked, no repository) append nothing. Payload is {path, bytes, sha256} of the bytes now on disk.
